title: The Case of the Besieged Detective Agency
notes: Case spans episodes 648-650 but only 648 and 650 subtitle files exist locally (0649.txt is missing from subs_resolved); the framing/hostage-negotiation scenes and any content unique to 649 could not be read, so this rebuild is based on 648 (setup: hostage-taking, evidence dump, SNS dying-message reveal) and 650 (resolution: false suicide bluff, true culprit reveal, confession) only. Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan/Kudo Shin'ichi, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, and new-this-episode Masumi Sera) omitted by convention, per CONSTRUCTION.md -- none of them are suspects, victims, or motive-holders in the underlying murder; Sera's only function is a red-herring subplot about Ran being seen with 'a guy', unrelated to the murder graph. Unlike several other rebuilds, the OLD case file's stated culprit (s2 = Shinobu Yuchi) is CORRECT and matches the transcript -- Yuchi (nicknamed 'Fox') is confirmed the killer in 650, not Mitsui ('Rat'), who was the initial red-herring suspect purely because she was literally the last of the three to visit Miku's room per the dying-message order. The old file's event order (Nihei, then Yuchi, then Mitsui visit the room) also matches. What the old file flattened: the SNS dying-message decoding required a second layer (the post ending on Fox's visit with 'still here... getting sleepy' was written before Rat/Mitsui ever arrived, meaning the last person actually in the room before Miku fell asleep was Fox, not the literal last visitor Rat); the physical evidence trail (filed book fore-edge hiding bloodied fingerprints, swapped bath slippers); and Yuchi's real motive (she ghostwrote/co-wrote Miku's award-winning debut novel and was denied credit, offered only an anonymous ghostwriter role going forward). No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. Multigraph: multiple parallel edges exist between the same node pairs (e.g. Yuchi->Miku carries both `kills` and `has_motive_against` and a prior `relationship`). Temporal fields (order/temporal_frame/years_before_present) intentionally omitted per current build guidance. case_type: murder.
